column1: # MODE: PROD
# Which artifacts belong to which integration mode.
# A skill that offers more than one way to be driven declares it here, and
# `install.sh --integration <skill>=<mode>` picks one without a prompt, so an
# agent can choose its own interface headlessly.
# The rule is deliberately narrow: a binary named below installs ONLY in its
# mode, and every file not named installs in every mode. So SKILL.md, the
# requirements table and the binaries registry are never mode-dependent.
# `skill` is the default, because it is the interface that needs no client
# configuration -- which is what a `curl | bash` install has to leave working.
# `mcp` is opt-in: its tools are listed in every session that configures the
# server, so it is worth choosing rather than assuming.
# chat-server-rs is deliberately UNLISTED, not `skill`-only. Somebody has to
# run the server, and in mcp mode that somebody is the same agent: the adapter
# finds a server and refuses to guess a port, but it does not start one. An
# mcp-only install with no server binary would be an install that can only ever
# join a channel somebody else's install created.
# chat-mcp needs no chat-client-rs beside it: the client is a LIBRARY it links,
# not a process it spawns, so discovery, the TOFU pin and the session are the
# same code either way. What a `skill`-mode install keeps that an mcp one gives
# up is the CLI's own maintenance path -- `read --local`, which walks the
# channel log with no server at all.
mode
skill
